subject: general
question: Which missile was successfully flight-trialed by DRDO and the Indian Navy from Integrated Test Range, Chandipur, Odisha, in 2025, demonstrating capability against ship targets when launched from a Sea King helicopter?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Naval Anti-Ship Missile - Short Range**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and the Indian Navy successfully flight-tested the **Naval Anti-Ship Missile - Short Range (NASM-SR)** in 2025.
 
• The missile was launched from a **Sea King helicopter** at the Integrated Test Range (ITR), Chandipur, Odisha.
 
• This indigenously developed missile demonstrated its capability to **engage ship targets effectively**, marking a significant milestone in India's defense technology.
 
• The NASM-SR is designed to enhance India’s maritime strike capabilities and ensures advanced defense capabilities for the Navy.
 
• The missile is equipped with modern technologies, including an **advanced navigation system and precision guidance**, ensuring high accuracy and reliability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **BrahMos Anti-Ship Missile**

 
 
• The BrahMos is a **supersonic cruise missile** developed jointly by India and Russia.
 
• It is capable of being launched from submarines, ships, aircraft, or land platforms.
 
• BrahMos has a range of 290 km (upgraded to 450-500 km in newer versions) and can carry a conventional warhead of 200–300 kg.
 
• Its supersonic speed (Mach 2.8 to 3.0) makes it one of the fastest cruise missiles in the world.
 
 
 
• **Prithvi Surface-to-Surface Missile**
 
 
• The Prithvi missile is part of India’s **Integrated Guided Missile Development Program (IGMDP)**.
 
• It is a short-range surface-to-surface ballistic missile with a range of 150-350 km depending on the variant.
 
• Prithvi is capable of carrying a nuclear or conventional warhead of up to 1,000 kg.
 
• It uses liquid propulsion and is primarily used by the Indian Army.
 
 
 
• **Agni Ballistic Missile**
 
 
• The Agni missile series is a family of **medium to intercontinental-range ballistic missiles** developed by DRDO.
 
• Agni missiles, such as Agni-I to Agni-VI, have ranges varying from 700 km to over 10,000 km.
 
• They are nuclear-capable and serve as a vital component of India’s strategic defense and deterrence capability.
 
• Agni-V is India’s first intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) with a range of over 5,000 km.
 
 
 
• **Missile Development in India**
 
 
• India has been actively developing indigenous missile systems to strengthen its defense capabilities under DRDO’s guidance.
 
• Key missile programs include the BrahMos, Agni, Prithvi, Akash, and Nag series, along with newer developments like NASM-SR.
